html:
In 335 BCE Alexander the Great took the Greek city of Thebes by storm and razed it to the ground.

Alexander had become king the year before. While he was campaigning far to the north in Illyria and Thrace, a rumour spread that he was dead. Thebes, which had lost its power at the Battle of Chaeronea, rose up and besieged the Macedonian garrison in its citadel. Alexander marched south so fast that he was at the walls within about two weeks. The Thebans refused to surrender, and the city was taken after hard fighting.

Alexander left the decision on Thebes to his Greek allies in the League of Corinth, many of whom hated it. The city was destroyed and its surviving people sold as slaves. Only the temples and the house of the poet Pindar were spared. The rest of Greece took the lesson: Athens quickly made peace, and Greece stayed quiet while Alexander invaded Persia. Thebes was rebuilt by Cassander twenty years later.
sum: In 335 BCE Alexander the Great took the Greek city of Thebes by storm and razed it to the ground.
